Hi Bryan & Sarah,

Great — provisioning the 7-day eval key now. Below are the technical notes tailored to your 50 rps / 150 burst profile: 

Endpoints and sample quickstart:
- Chat (conversational): POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions
- Embeddings: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings

Example curl (replace <EVAL_KEY>):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \n    -H \"Authorization: Bearer <EVAL_KEY>\" \n    -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n    -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-1.1\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Hello\"}],\"max_tokens\":150}'

Rate limits & throughput guidance:
- Eval key soft limits (default): 200 rps account-level soft limit. For your PoC we recommend configuring sustained concurrency to ~50-100 connections and allow bursts up to 250 for short windows.
- Per-token latency: on our hosted fleet redwood-1.1 typically generates at ~8-12ms per token. With your 120-token average payload expect ~1.0-1.5s server-side generation time; add network/client overhead.
- Best practices: use keep-alive, limit inflight requests per connection to 1-2, and implement client-side backoff for 429/503. Redwood returns Retry-After and X-RateLimit-Remaining headers on throttled responses.

Auth & key rotation:
- Eval key: time-bound 7-day key (scoped to your test workspace).
- Rotation: production keys can be rotated via the Console or API. We support short-lived keys issued by your secrets manager for long-term deployments.

Observability:
- Console shows per-request token counts, latencies and cost. For the PoC we'll enable extended logs and a shared trace link so your team can correlate requests.

I'll send the eval key and a small Python + curl test script in a separate email. If you anticipate sustained load above the burst window for >10 minutes, tell us expected window and we can temporarily raise soft limits for the PoC.

Regards,
